about.title: El Centro Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical care in El Centro runs through a small circle of clinics and hospitals serving Imperial County, and when something goes sideways during treatment, patients often don't know where to turn. Maybe a surgical step was skipped, a lab result was overlooked, or a medication order didn't match the chart. California law treats these claims differently than a car crash — there's a shorter window to act, a required 90-day notice before filing suit, and a rule that a bad medical outcome by itself doesn't prove negligence occurred. That's why an early conversation with someone who understands these cases matters. We handle medical malpractice claims in Imperial County and can review what happened and explain your options under California's medical malpractice rules, including the notice requirement and the expert-review standard that applies to nearly every case like this.

whyChoose.title: Why El Centro Patients Reach Out Early

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You'd Think
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to sort out what happened can quietly cost you that window.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the law requires a 90-day notice to the provider. Our team is familiar with this step and can help make sure it's handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California cases typically need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was broken. We can help arrange that kind of review before deciding how to move forward.

items.question: Is every bad medical outcome considered malpractice in California?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't establish negligence. There has to be evidence that a provider departed from the accepted standard of care, which is why expert review is such a central part of these claims.

items.question: Are there fewer malpractice attorneys near El Centro because of the smaller Imperial County market?
items.answer: El Centro doesn't have the density of specialized malpractice attorneys you'd find in a larger metro area, which is one reason people often widen their search. We handle these cases and can help even if you're in Imperial County.

items.question: Is California's cap on damages the same every year?
items.answer: No — the statutory cap on non-economic damages under MICRA is set to rise annually. We can walk you through how the current cap applies to your specific situation.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. You can discuss the fee arrangement directly with us during your consultation.
